verses.zh: 有一日，扫罗的儿子约拿单对拿他兵器的少年人说：「我们不如过到那边，到非利士人的防营那里去。」但他没有告诉父亲。
verses.en: Then one day Jonathan son of Saul said to his armor-bearer,[NOTE:1] “Come on, let’s go over to the Philistine garrison that is opposite us.” But he did not let his father know.
notes: Or “the servant who was carrying his military equipment” (likewise in vv. 6, 7, 12, 13, 14).
verses.commentary: 14:1 Jonathan takes the initiative and attacks a Philistine outpost.

verses.zh: 扫罗在基比亚的尽边，坐在米矶仑的石榴树下，跟随他的约有六百人。
verses.en: Now Saul was sitting under a pomegranate tree in Migron, on the outskirts of Gibeah. The army that was with him numbered about 600 men.
verses.commentary:
14:2 This is a very detailed account. It was obviously an eye-witness report (i.e., vv. 4-5,14).

Notice Saul had only 600 soldiers left (cf. 1 Sam. 13:15).

verses.zh: 在那里有亚希突的儿子亚希亚，穿着以弗得。（亚希突是以迦博的哥哥，非尼哈的儿子，以利的孙子。以利从前在示罗作耶和华的祭司。）约拿单去了，百姓却不知道。
verses.en: Now Ahijah was carrying[NOTE:1] an ephod. He was the son of Ahitub, who was the brother of Ichabod and a son of Phinehas, son of Eli, the priest of the Lord in Shiloh. The army was unaware that Jonathan had left.
notes: Heb “bearing.” Many English versions understand this verb to mean “wearing” (cf. KJV, NAB, NASB, NIV, NLT). The ephod could be used for consulting the Lord’s will (1 Sam 23:9-10; 30:7-8) and is not always worn (1 Sam 23:6). The significance in this context is probably not that Ahijah was dressed for sacrificial duties or to appear before God at the tabernacle, but rather that the ephod was available for consulting God, given the people’s ignorance about Jonathan’s activities. (Cf. the note at 1 Sam 2:28.)
verses.commentary:
14:3 There was a priestly representative with Saul.

▣ "wearing the ephod" This was a special outer robe of the High Priest which had a pocket with the
Urim and Thummim.

▣ The LXX thinks that the "ark" mentioned in v. 18 was, in reality, the "ephod."

SPECIAL TOPIC: EPHOD

SPECIAL TOPIC: URIM AND THUMMIM

verses.zh: 约拿单要从隘口过到非利士防营那里去。这隘口两边各有一个山峰：一名播薛，一名西尼；
verses.en: Now there was a steep cliff on each side of the pass through which Jonathan intended to go to reach the Philistine garrison. One cliff was named Bozez, the other Seneh.
verses.commentary:
14:4-5

NASB, NKJV
"between the passes"

NRSV, NJB, REB
"in the pass"

JPSOA
"at the crossing"

LXX
"the middle of the pass"

Peshitta
"to cross over"

The MT has "between the passes." The JPSOA footnote says, "meaning of Hebrew uncertain."

The verse tries to clarify that there was a "sharp crag" on each side of a natural pass. The
Philistines had the high ground.

verses.zh: 一峰向北，与密抹相对，一峰向南，与迦巴相对。
verses.en: The cliff to the north was closer to Micmash, the one to the south closer to Geba.

verses.zh: 约拿单对拿兵器的少年人说：「我们不如过到未受割礼人的防营那里去，或者耶和华为我们施展能力；因为耶和华使人得胜，不在乎人多人少。」
verses.en: Jonathan said to his armor-bearer, “Come on, let’s go over to the garrison of these uncircumcised men. Perhaps the Lord will intervene[NOTE:1] for us. Nothing can prevent the Lord from delivering, whether by many or by a few.”
notes: Heb “act.”
verses.commentary:
14:6 "these uncircumcised" This was an idiom of derision (cf. 1 Sam. 17:26,36). The Philistines being
from the Aegean Islands (i.e., Greek culture) were the only people of the region not circumcised. Other ANE
cultures did it at different times but all did it.

For a good brief discussion, see Roland deVaux, Ancient Israel, pp. 46-48.

▣ "perhaps the Lord will work for us" This act of faith illustrates
Jonathan's trust in YHWH, but without demanding the result (much like Daniel 3).

verses.zh: 拿兵器的对他说：「随你的心意行吧。你可以上去，我必跟随你，与你同心。」
verses.en: His armor-bearer said to him, “Do everything that is on your mind.[NOTE:1] Do as you’re inclined. I’m with you all the way!”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “in your heart.”
Heb “Look, I am with you, according to your heart.” See the note at 13:14.
verses.commentary:
14:7

NASB
"turn yourself"

NKJV
"Go then"

JPSOA
"You go first"

REB
"go ahead"

LXX
"do all that your mind inclines to"

Peshitta
"turn aside"

The MT has "do all that is in your mind, incline to yourself." It is the last phrase that has
caused the divergence in translations (BDB 639, KB 692,Qal IMPERATIVE). This
VERB can mean

- stretch out, 2 Sam. 6:17

- spread out, 2 Sam. 6:17; 21:10

- extend

- incline, here (incline the heart)

- bend, turn, cf. Num. 21:15; 22:23; 1 Sam. 8:3; 2 Sam. 2:19; 22:10

- Hiphil, "take an aside," 2 Sam. 3:27; 6:10

The UBS Text Project, p. 176, gives the MT a "B" rating (some doubt). It supports the NEB translation,
"do what you will, go forward."

verses.zh: 约拿单说：「我们要过到那些人那里去，使他们看见我们。
verses.en: Jonathan replied, “All right.[NOTE:1] We’ll go over to these men and fight them.
notes: Heb “Look!”
verses.commentary:
14:8-11 Jonathan is proposing a sign from YHWH that his venture will be successful, similar to

- Israel's servant in Genesis 24

- Gideon in Judges 6

- Samuel's sign to Israel in 1 Sam. 12:16-18

verses.zh: 他们若对我们说：『你们站住，等我们到你们那里去』，我们就站住，不上他们那里去。
verses.en: If they say to us, ‘Stay put until we approach you,’ we will stay[NOTE:1] right there and not go up to them.
notes: Heb “stand.”

verses.zh: 他们若说：『你们上到我们这里来』，这话就是我们的证据；我们便上去，因为耶和华将他们交在我们手里了。」
verses.en: But if they say, ‘Come up against us,’ we will go up. For in that case the Lord has given them into our hand—it will be a sign to us.”

verses.zh: 二人就使非利士的防兵看见。非利士人说：「希伯来人从所藏的洞穴里出来了！」
verses.en: When they[NOTE:1] made themselves known to the Philistine garrison, the Philistines said, “Look! The Hebrews are coming out of the holes in which they hid themselves.”
notes: Heb “the two of them.”
verses.commentary: 14:11 The Philistines are ridiculing the faithless retreat and hiding of the Israelites from 1 Sam. 13:6-7.

verses.zh: 防兵对约拿单和拿兵器的人说：「你们上到这里来，我们有一件事指示你们。」约拿单就对拿兵器的人说：「你跟随我上去，因为耶和华将他们交在以色列人手里了。」
verses.en: Then the men of the garrison said to Jonathan and his armor-bearer, “Come on up to us so we can teach you a thing or two!”[NOTE:1] Then Jonathan said to his armor-bearer, “Come up behind me, for the Lord has given[NOTE:2] them into the hand of Israel!”
notes: Heb “a thing.”
The perfect verbal form is used rhetorically here to express Jonathan’s certitude. As far as he is concerned, the victory is as good as won and can be described as such.
verses.commentary:
14:12 "into the hands of. . ." This is an idiom of victory.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND

verses.zh: 约拿单就爬上去，拿兵器的人跟随他。约拿单杀倒非利士人，拿兵器的人也随着杀他们。
verses.en: Jonathan crawled up on his hands and feet, with his armor-bearer following behind him. Jonathan struck down the Philistines,[NOTE:1] while his armor-bearer came along behind him and killed them.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and they fell before Jonathan.”
Heb “and the one carrying his equipment was killing after him.”
verses.commentary:
14:13 "climbed up on his hands and feet" This shows the high and defensible outpost of the Philistines.
It would have seemed impossible to attack this position from this direction!

▣ "fell. . .killed" This interpretive question is, "Does this phrase refer to a two stage attack (TEV)
or just parallel VERBS?" The Knox translation has "some fell to Jonathan himself, and some to the
squire as he came up behind him." The UBS Handbook, p. 279, has an interesting suggestion. "Jonathan
killed the Philistines who attacked from the front, and the soldier killed those who attacked from behind."

verses.zh: 约拿单和拿兵器的人起头所杀的约有二十人，都在一亩地的半犁沟之内。
verses.en: In this initial skirmish Jonathan and his armor-bearer struck down about 20 men in an area that measured half an acre.
verses.commentary:
14:14

NASB, NRSV
"within about half a furrow in an acre of land"

NKJV
"within about half an acre of land"

NKJV footnote
"half the area plowed by a yoke"

TEV
"in an area about half an acre"

NJB
—omit—

REB
"like men cutting a furrow across a half-acre field"

JPSOA
"within a space about half a furrow long (in) an acre of land"

LXX
"with darts and sling stones and with pebbles of the plain"

Peshitta
"they cut them to pieces like stone-cutters and like men who plough a field"

Obviously the MT is obscure. The theories range from

- time (half the time of plowing, NKJV footnote)

- space (JPSOA)

- means (LXX, Peshitta)

verses.zh: 于是在营中、在田野、在众民内都有战兢，防兵和掠兵也都战兢，地也震动，战兢之势甚大。
verses.en: Then fear overwhelmed[NOTE:1] those who were in the camp, those who were in the field, all the army in the garrison, and the raiding bands. They trembled and the ground shook. This fear was caused by God.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “fell upon.”

Heb “and it was by the fear of God.” The translation understands this to mean that God was the source or cause of the fear experienced by the Philistines. This seems to be the most straightforward reading of the sentence. It is possible, however, that the word “God” functions here simply to intensify the accompanying word “fear,” in which one might translate “a very great fear” (cf. NAB, NRSV). It is clear that on some occasions that the divine name carries such a superlative nuance. For examples see Joüon 2:525 §141.n.
verses.commentary:
14:15 As the Israelites had feared and trembled, so now the Philistines.

- those in the army

- those in the field

- all the people

- the raiders of 1 Sam. 13:17-18

▣

NASB
"a great trembling"

NKJV
"a very great trembling"

NRSV, TEV, REB
"a very great panic"

NJB
"a panic from YHWH"

JPSOA
"a terror from God"

LXX
"a dread was from the Lord"

Peshitta
"the fear of the Lord"

The difference between

- great (BDB 43) ‒ אל

- God (BDB 43) ‒ אלהים

is the question of how to translate "Elohim" in the context.

▣ "trembling" This VERB (BDB 353, KB 350, Qal PERFECT)
denotes "terror," "fear," "physical trembling"

- in YHWH's presence ‒ Exod. 19:16,18 (i.e., Mt. Sinai)

- in the day of judgment ‒ Isa. 10:29; 19:16; 32:11; 41:5

- in battle

- Saul's army ‒ 1 Sam. 13:7

- Philistine army ‒ 1 Sam. 14:15

- Saul himself ‒ 1 Sam. 28:5

- hope of Ahithophel concerning David's army ‒ 2 Sam. 17:2

- in bad news ‒ 1 Sam. 16:4; 21:1

verses.zh: 在便雅悯的基比亚，扫罗的守望兵看见非利士的军众溃散，四围乱窜。
verses.en: Saul’s watchmen at Gibeah in the territory of Benjamin[NOTE:1] looked on[NOTE:2] as the crowd of soldiers seemed to melt away first in one direction and then in another.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “at Gibeah of Benjamin.” The words “in the territory” are supplied in the translation for clarity.
Heb “saw, and look!”
Heb “the crowd melted and went, even here.”
verses.commentary: 14:16 This must refer to the Philistine soldiers (cf. v. 15).

verses.zh: 扫罗就对跟随他的民说：「你们查点查点，看从我们这里出去的是谁？」他们一查点，就知道约拿单和拿兵器的人没有在这里。
verses.en: So Saul said to the army that was with him, “Muster the troops and see who is no longer with us.” When they mustered the troops,[NOTE:1] Jonathan and his armor-bearer were not there.
notes: Heb “and they mustered the troops, and look!”

verses.zh: 那时　神的约柜在以色列人那里。扫罗对亚希亚说：「你将　神的约柜运了来。」
verses.en: So Saul said to Ahijah, “Bring near the ephod,”[NOTE:1] for he was at that time wearing the ephod in front of the Israelites.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the ark of God.” It seems unlikely that Saul would call for the ark, which was several miles away in Kiriath Jearim (see 1 Sam 7:2). The LXX and an Old Latin ms have “ephod” here, a reading which harmonizes better with v. 3 and fits better with the verb “bring near” (see 1 Sam 23:9; 30:7) and with the expression “withdraw your hand” in v. 19. There are also quotations of this reading in rabbinic literature and medieval Jewish literature according to V. Aptowitzer, The Scripture in the Rabbinic Literature and Medieval Jewish Literature, Prolegomena (3 parts, Vindobonae, 1906, 1908, 1911). It is followed in the present translation (cf. NAB, NJB, GWN, TEV, NLT, CEB, BBE).
Heb “for the ark of God was in that day, and the sons of Israel.” The translation follows the text of some Greek manuscripts. See the previous note.
verses.commentary:
14:18 "bring the ark of God" Again, like verse 3, the LXX sees this as "the ephod" (NET). Earlier, the Israelite
army in Eli's day took the ark into battle and lost it.

However, here Saul wants to consult YHWH, but this was not done by the ark but the Urim and
Thummim in the ephod of the High Priest. The VERB (BDB 620, KB 670, Hiphil
IMPERATIVE) is never used of the ark, but often of priests (i.e., the ephod, cf. 1 Sam. 23:9;
30:7).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE ARK OF THE COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: URIM AND THUMMIM

verses.zh: 扫罗正与祭司说话的时候，非利士营中的喧嚷越发大了；扫罗就对祭司说：「停手吧！」
verses.en: While[NOTE:1] Saul spoke to the priest, the panic in the Philistines’ camp was becoming greater and greater. So Saul said to the priest, “Withdraw your hand.”
notes: Or perhaps “until.”
verses.commentary:
14:19 It seems as Saul was consulting the priest with no response that he noticed the commotion in the
Philistine ranks. At that point he stops the priestly act (i.e., "withdraw your hand") and attacks without waiting on YHWH
(i.e., the second time).

▣ "increased" This is an INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and IMPERFECT VERB
of the same root (BDB 229, KB 246, Qal) which denotes intensity.

verses.zh: 扫罗和跟随他的人都聚集，来到战场，看见非利士人用刀互相击杀，大大惶乱。
verses.en: Saul and all the army assembled and marched into battle, where they found[NOTE:1] the Philistines in total panic killing one another with their swords.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and look, there was.”
Heb “the sword of a man against his companion, a very great panic.”
verses.commentary:
14:20 This verse uses "holy war" terminology to show that YHWH was aiding the Israelites, as

- during the Exodus, Exod. 23:27

- during the Conquest, Deut. 2:25; 7:23; Josh. 1:9; 2:9; 10:10

- during the time of Gideon, Jdgs. 7:22

- in Samuel's day, 1 Sam. 7:10; here (and v. 15).

▣

NASB, NRSV
"rallied"

NKJV
"assembled"

TEV
"marched"

NJB
"form up and advanced"

REB
"made a concerted rush"

JPSOA
"assembled and rushed"

LXX
"went up"

Peshitta
"shouted"

The VERB (BDB 277, KB 277, Niphal IMPERFECT
with waw) can mean

- assemble (i.e., "call together," here)

- cry out

- battle cry or muster (2 Sam. 20:4-5)

- prayer (1 Sam. 7:8-9; 8:18; 12:8,10; 15:11)

- grieving (1 Sam. 4:13; 5:10; 2 Sam. 13:19; 19:5)

- complain (2 Sam. 19:28)

verses.zh: 从前由四方来跟随非利士军的希伯来人现在也转过来，帮助跟随扫罗和约拿单的以色列人了。
verses.en: The Hebrews who had earlier gone over to the Philistine side[NOTE:1] joined the Israelites who were with Saul and Jonathan.
notes: Heb “and the Hebrews were to the Philistines formerly, who went up with them in the camp all around.”
verses.commentary:
14:21 "the Hebrews who were with the Philistines previously" Apparently some Hebrews

- hid, 1 Sam. 13:6; 14:22

- fled, 1 Sam. 13:7

- surrendered earlier

- became mercenary soldiers

- sold themselves as slaves (see Roland deVaux, Ancient Israel, p. 83)

verses.zh: 那藏在以法莲山地的以色列人听说非利士人逃跑，就出来紧紧地追杀他们。
verses.en: When all the Israelites who had hidden themselves in the hill country of Ephraim heard that the Philistines had fled, they too pursued them in battle.

verses.zh: 那日，耶和华使以色列人得胜，一直战到伯・亚文。
verses.en: So the Lord delivered Israel that day, and the battle shifted over to Beth Aven.[NOTE:1]
notes: The LXX includes the following words: “And all the people were with Saul, about ten thousand men. And the battle extended to the entire city on mount Ephraim.”
verses.commentary: 14:23 The victory was YHWH's victory (i.e., holy war).

verses.zh: 扫罗叫百姓起誓说，凡不等到晚上向敌人报完了仇吃甚么的，必受咒诅。因此这日百姓没有吃甚么，就极其困惫。
verses.en: Now the men of Israel were hard pressed that day, for Saul had made the army agree to this oath: “Cursed be the man who eats food before evening. I will get my vengeance on my enemies!” So no one in the army ate anything.
verses.commentary:
14:24 This vow, like Jephthah, Judges 11, was ill advised and inappropriate, but it was still a vow in YHWH's
name (i.e., Leviticus 27).

verses.zh: 众民进入树林，见有蜜在地上。
verses.en: Now the whole army[NOTE:1] entered the forest, and there was honey on the ground.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “all the land.”
Heb “the surface of the field.”

verses.zh: 他们进了树林，见有蜜流下来，却没有人敢用手取蜜入口，因为他们怕那誓言。
verses.en: When the army entered the forest, they saw[NOTE:1] the honey flowing, but no one ate any of it,[NOTE:2] for the army was afraid of the oath.
notes: Heb “and the army entered the forest, and look!”
Heb “and there was no one putting his hand to his mouth.”

verses.zh: 约拿单没有听见他父亲叫百姓起誓，所以伸手中的杖，用杖头蘸在蜂房里，转手送入口内，眼睛就明亮了。
verses.en: But Jonathan had not heard about the oath his father had made the army take. He extended the end of his staff that was in his hand and dipped it in the honeycomb. When he ate it,[NOTE:1] his eyes gleamed.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and he returned his hand to his mouth.”
The translation follows the Qere and several medieval Hebrew mss in reading “gleamed,” rather than the Kethib, “saw.”
verses.commentary:
14:27

NASB, NRSV, Peshitta
"his eyes brightened"

NKJV
"his countenance brightened"

TEV
"he felt better"

NJB
"his eyes grew brighter"

REB
"was refreshed"

JPSOA
"his eyes lit up"

LXX
"his eyes recovered their sight"

NET
"his eyes gleamed"

The MT has the VERB "see" (BDB 906, KB 1157, Qal IMPERFECT
with waw), but most modern translations follow the Qere (i.e., the suggestion of the
Masoretic scholars) "be bright" (BDB 21, KB 24, Qal
IMPERFECT with waw).

The idiom has two connotations.

- bring truth or insight ‒ Ps. 19:28; 19:8; 36:9

- refresh physically ‒ 1 Sam. 14:28b-29; Ezra 9:8; Ps. 13:3

Here, option #2 fits best.

verses.zh: 百姓中有一人对他说：「你父亲曾叫百姓严严地起誓说，今日吃甚么的，必受咒诅；因此百姓就疲乏了。」
verses.en: Then someone from the army informed him, “Your father put the army under a strict oath[NOTE:1] saying, ‘Cursed be the man who eats food today.’ That is why the army is tired.”
notes: Heb “your father surely put the army under an oath.” The infinitive absolute is used before the finite verb to emphasize the solemn nature of the oath.
verses.commentary:
14:28 "strictly. . .under oath" This is an INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and a PERFECT VERB
from the same root (BDB 989, KB 1396) which denotes intensity.

Jonathan expresses his negative opinion of this father's oath in vv. 28-30.

▣ "the people were weary" This is repeated in verse 31.

verses.zh: 约拿单说：「我父亲连累你们了。你看，我尝了这一点蜜，眼睛就明亮了。
verses.en: Then Jonathan said, “My father has caused trouble for the land. See how my eyes gleamed[NOTE:1] when I tasted just a little of this honey.
notes: The LXX reads “saw.” See v. 27.

verses.zh: 今日百姓若任意吃了从仇敌所夺的物，击杀的非利士人岂不更多吗？」
verses.en: Certainly if the army had eaten some of the enemies’ provisions that they came across today, would not the slaughter of the Philistines have been even greater?”
verses.commentary:
14:30 "eaten freely" This is another intensified form (i.e., INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and a
PERFECT VERB of the same root, BDB 37, KB 46).

verses.zh: 这日，以色列人击杀非利士人，从密抹直到亚雅仑。百姓甚是疲乏，
verses.en: On that day the army struck down the Philistines from Micmash to Aijalon, and they became very tired.

verses.zh: 就急忙将所夺的牛羊和牛犊宰于地上，肉还带血就吃了。
verses.en: So the army rushed greedily on[NOTE:1] the[NOTE:2] plunder, confiscating sheep, cattle, and calves. They slaughtered them right on the ground, and the army ate them, blood and all.
notes: The translation follows the Qere and many medieval Hebrew mss in reading “and they rushed greedily upon,” rather than the Kethib, “and they did.”
The translation reads with the Qere and many medieval Hebrew mss הַשָּׁלָל (hashalal, “the spoil”) rather than following the Kethib reading, שָׁלָל (shalal, “spoil”).
verses.commentary:
14:32

NASB, Peshitta
"rushed greedily"

NKJV, TEV
"rushed"

NRSV
"flew upon"

NJB
"flung themselves"

REB
"seized"

JPSOA
"pounced on"

LXX
"turned to"

The MT has the VERB (BDB 793, KB 889, Qal IMPERFECT
with waw) which is the common word for "do" or "make." The Masoretic scholars (Qere) suggested an emendation
to BDB 743, KB 816, Qal IMPERFECT with waw, which has the intensified meaning of "dart greedily."
This fits the context better.

- do ‒ עשׂה (BDB 793 I)

- dart greedily ‒ עיט (BDB 743)

The implied excuse for the conscripted soldiers eating meat with blood in it was

- they were tired

- they had not eaten anything since morning because of Saul's rash vow

This was a specific covenant violation (cf. Lev. 7:26-27; 17:10-14; 19:26) and even before Moses (i.e., Gen. 9:4).

SPECIAL TOPIC: BLOOD

verses.zh: 有人告诉扫罗说：「百姓吃带血的肉，得罪耶和华了。」扫罗说：「你们有罪了，今日要将大石头滚到我这里来。」
verses.en: Now it was reported to Saul, “Look, the army is sinning against the Lord by eating even the blood.” He said, “All of you have broken the covenant![NOTE:1] Roll a large stone over here[NOTE:2] to me.”
notes: Heb “You have acted deceptively.” In this context the verb refers to violating an agreement, in this case the dietary and sacrificial regulations of the Mosaic law. The verb form is second masculine plural; apparently Saul here addresses those who are eating the animals.
The translation follows the LXX reading ἐνταῦθα (entautha, “here”) for הֲלֹם (halom, “here”) rather than the MT’s הַיּוֹם (hayyom, “today”).
verses.commentary:
14:33 Saul recognized the seriousness of the covenant violations. His response was to offer an immediate peace
sacrifice. Apparently the High Priest of vv. 3,18 was still there.

Because of v. 34, possibly there were several priests present (cf. v. 36c).

verses.zh: 扫罗又说：「你们散在百姓中，对他们说，你们各人将牛羊牵到我这里来宰了吃，不可吃带血的肉得罪耶和华。」这夜，百姓就把牛羊牵到那里宰了。
verses.en: Then Saul said, “Scatter out among the army and say to them, ‘Each of you bring to me your ox and sheep and slaughter them in this spot and eat. But don’t sin against the Lord by eating the blood.’” So that night each one brought his ox and slaughtered it there.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and all the army brought near, each his ox by his hand, and they slaughtered there.”

verses.zh: 扫罗为耶和华筑了一座坛，这是他初次为耶和华筑的坛。
verses.en: Then Saul built an altar for the Lord; it was the first time he had built an altar for the Lord.
verses.commentary: 14:35 This altar refers to the large stone of v. 33. Usually Samuel built the altar (cf. 1 Sam.7:12,17).

verses.zh: 扫罗说：「我们不如夜里下去追赶非利士人，抢掠他们，直到天亮，不留他们一人。」众民说：「你看怎样好就去行吧！」祭司说：「我们先当亲近　神。」
verses.en: Saul said, “Let’s go down after the Philistines at night; we will rout[NOTE:1] them until the break of day.[NOTE:2] We won’t leave any of them alive!”[NOTE:3] They replied, “Do whatever seems best to you.”[NOTE:4] But the priest said, “Let’s approach God here.”
notes: Heb “plunder.”
Heb “until the light of the morning.”
Heb “and there will not be left among them a man.”
Heb “all that is good in your eyes.” So also in v. 40.

verses.zh: 扫罗求问　神说：「我下去追赶非利士人可以不可以？你将他们交在以色列人手里不交？」这日　神没有回答他。
verses.en: So Saul asked God, “Should I go down after the Philistines? Will you deliver them into the hand of Israel?” But he did not answer him that day.
verses.commentary: 14:37 YHWH did not answer Saul. Saul took this as being because Jonathan had broken the oath.

verses.zh: 扫罗说：「你们百姓中的长老都上这里来，查明今日是谁犯了罪。
verses.en: Then Saul said, “All you leaders of the army come here. Find out[NOTE:1] how this sin occurred today.
notes: Heb “know and see.”
verses.commentary:
14:38

NASB, NKJV
"chiefs"

NRSV, TEV, NJB, REB, LXX
"leaders"

JPSOA
"chief officers"

Peshitta
"families"

The MT has a FEMININE PLURAL NOUN (BDB 819, KB 945) which is used in the
sense of leaders only three times (i.e., Jdgs. 20:2; 1 Sam. 14:38; Isa. 19:13). Its etymology suggests an idiom from
"the corner-tower" (KB 945, Zeph. 3:6).

When a rare word such as this is used, one wonders

- does it have a specialized connotation

- was it used for literary variety

- is it from a different yet unknown Semitic root?

verses.zh: 我指着救以色列―永生的耶和华起誓，就是我儿子约拿单犯了罪，他也必死。」但百姓中无一人回答他。
verses.en: For as surely as the Lord, the deliverer of Israel, lives, even if it turns out to be my own son Jonathan, he will certainly die!” But no one from the army said anything.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and there was no one answering from all the army.”
verses.commentary:
14:39 "as the Lord lives" This is a play on the VERB "to be" and
the covenant name for Deity, YHWH, which is a form of that VERB.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ "he shall surely die" This is another intensified grammatical form (i.e., an INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE
and an IMPERFECT VERB of the same root, BDB 559, KB 562).

verses.zh: 扫罗就对以色列众人说：「你们站在一边，我与我儿子约拿单也站在一边。」百姓对扫罗说：「你看怎样好就去行吧！」
verses.en: Then he said to all Israel, “You will be on one side, and I and my son Jonathan will be on the other side.” The army replied to Saul, “Do whatever you think is best.”
verses.commentary:
14:40-41 Saul is not sure if the sin that caused YHWH to be silent was

- his oath and Jonathan's violation

- the people eating meat with blood

verses.zh: 扫罗祷告耶和华―以色列的　神说：「求你指示实情。」于是掣签掣出扫罗和约拿单来；百姓尽都无事。
verses.en: Then Saul said, “O Lord God of Israel! If this sin has been committed by me or by my son Jonathan, then, O Lord God of Israel, respond with Urim.[NOTE:1] But if this sin has been committed by your people Israel, respond with Thummim.”[NOTE:2] Then Jonathan and Saul were indicated by lot, while the army was exonerated.[NOTE:3]
notes: The Urim and Thummim were used for lot casting in ancient Israel. Their exact identity is uncertain; they may have been specially marked stones drawn from a bag. See Exod 28:30; Lev 8:8, and Deut 33:8, as well as the discussion in R. W. Klein, 1 Samuel (WBC), 140. tc Heb “to the Lord God of Israel: ‘Give what is perfect.’” The Hebrew textual tradition has accidentally omitted several words here. The present translation follows the LXX (as do several English versions, cf. NAB, NRSV, TEV). See P. K. McCarter, I Samuel (AB), 247-48, and R. W. Klein, 1 Samuel (WBC), 132.
Heb “went out.”

The LXX includes the following words: “Whomever the Lord will indicate by the lot, let him die! And the people said to Saul, ‘It is not this word.’ But Saul prevailed over the people, and they cast lots between him and between Jonathan his son.”
verses.commentary:
14:41 "Give a perfect lot" This is expanded in the LXX, which is followed by NRSV, REB, as "If this guilt is in me
or in my son Jonathan, O Lord God of Israel, give Urim; but if the guilt is in your people Israel, give
Thummim.

verses.zh: 扫罗说：「你们再掣签，看是我，是我儿子约拿单」，就掣出约拿单来。
verses.en: Then Saul said, “Cast the lot between me and my son Jonathan!”[NOTE:1] Jonathan was indicated by lot.
notes: Heb “Look, I, I will die.” Apparently Jonathan is acquiescing to his anticipated fate of death (cf. NIV11 “And now I must die!”) . However, the words may be taken as sarcastic (“Here I am about to die!”) or as a question, “Must I now die?” (cf. NAB, NIV84, NCV, NLT).

verses.zh: 扫罗对约拿单说：「你告诉我，你做了甚么事？」约拿单说：「我实在以手里的杖，用杖头蘸了一点蜜尝了一尝。这样我就死吗（或译：吧！）？」
verses.en: So Saul said to Jonathan, “Tell me what you have done.” Jonathan told him, “I used the end of the staff that was in my hand to taste a little honey. I must die!”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “So God will do and so he will add, surely you will certainly die, Jonathan.”

verses.zh: 扫罗说：「约拿单哪，你定要死！若不然，愿　神重重地降罚与我。」
verses.en: Saul said, “God will punish me severely if Jonathan doesn’t die!”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and he did not die.”
verses.commentary:
14:44 YHWH identifies Jonathan as the reason for no answer to Saul's request for direction.

Saul's initial comment in v. 44 is a curse oath (cf. Ruth 1:17; 1 Sam. 3:17; 20:13; 25:22;
2 Sam. 3:9,35; 19:13; 1 Kgs. 2:23; 19:2; 20:10; 2 Kgs. 6:31) for disobedience.

▣ "you shall surely die" This is another intensified form, like v. 39.

verses.zh: 百姓对扫罗说：「约拿单在以色列人中这样大行拯救，岂可使他死呢？断乎不可！我们指着永生的耶和华起誓，连他的一根头发也不可落地，因为他今日与　神一同做事。」于是百姓救约拿单免了死亡。
verses.en: But the army said to Saul, “Should Jonathan, who won this great victory in Israel, die? May it never be! As surely as the Lord lives, not a single hair of his head will fall to the ground, for it is with the help of God that he has acted today.” So the army rescued Jonathan from death.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “to their place.”
verses.commentary:
14:45 This verse is surprising. YHWH showed His will by the lots. Saul affirmed his willingness to kill his
son but the Israelite people revolted!

It is unstated but apparently Jonathan's

- ignorance of his father's oath

- victory over the Philistines

- the people offering a sacrifice or paying a price

was sufficient grounds for YHWH to harken to the will of the people.

▣ "there shall not one hair of his head fall to the ground" This is an idiom for nothing happening to
Jonathan, not in any way his being punished for a rash oath he was ignorant of! It is also found in 2 Sam. 14:11 and 1 Kgs. 1:57.

▣

NASB, NKJV
"rescued"

NRSV, NJB
"ransomed"

TEV, JPSOA
"saved"

REB, Peshitta
"delivered"

LXX
"prayed"

The MT has the VERB "ransomed" (BDB 804, KB 911, Qal IMPERFECT
with waw). It is unstated how this was done.

SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM

verses.zh: 扫罗回去，不追赶非利士人；非利士人也回本地去了。
verses.en: Then Saul stopped chasing the Philistines, and the Philistines went back home.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “his,” which could refer to Israel or to Saul.
verses.commentary:
14:46 In light of

- no answer from YHWH, v. 37

- the people's revolt, v. 45

Saul did not continue the attack against the Philistines.

verses.zh: 扫罗执掌以色列的国权，常常攻击他四围的一切仇敌，就是摩押人、亚扪人、以东人，和琐巴诸王，并非利士人。他无论往何处去，都打败仇敌。
verses.en: After Saul had secured his royal position over Israel, he fought against all their[NOTE:1] enemies on all sides—the Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, the kings of Zobah, and the Philistines. In every direction that he turned, he was victorious.[NOTE:2]
notes: The translation follows the LXX (“he was delivered”), rather than the MT, which reads, “he acted wickedly.”
Heb “plunderers.”
verses.commentary:
14:47 "Zobah" This is the first mention of Israel attacking northward beyond her borders. This was an
Armenian/Syrian kingdom later attacked by David (cf. 2 Sam. 8:3-10).

verses.zh: 扫罗奋勇攻击亚玛力人，救了以色列人脱离抢掠他们之人的手。
verses.en: He fought bravely, striking down the Amalekites and delivering Israel from the hand of its enemies.[NOTE:1]
notes: The list differs from others. In 1 Sam 31:2 (= 1 Chr 10:2), Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malki-Shua are listed as Saul’s sons, while 1 Chr 8:33 and 9:39 list Jonathan, Malki-Shua, Abinadab, and Eshbaal.

verses.zh: 扫罗的儿子是约拿单、亦施韦、麦基舒亚。他的两个女儿：长女名米拉，次女名米甲。
verses.en: The sons of Saul were Jonathan, Ishvi, and Malki-Shua.[NOTE:1] He had two daughters; the older one was named Merab and the younger Michal.
notes: The word “uncle” can modify either Abner or Ner. See the note on the word “son” in v. 51 for further discussion.
verses.commentary:
14:49-51 This is a genealogy of Saul's family.

14:49

NASB, NRSV, TEV, NJB, JPSOA
"Ishvi"

NKJV
"Jishvi"

REB
"Ishyo"

LXX
"Iessiou"

Peshitta
"Ishui"

The MT has "Ishvi" ("man of YHWH," KB 446,
וישׁוי).

This person goes by several names.

- Ishvi (one of three sons), 1 Chr. 8:33 lists four sons

- Ish-bosheth ("man of shame," BDB 36), 2 Sam. 2:8; 3:8; 4:5

- Eshbaal ("man of Baal," BDB 36), 1 Chr. 8:33; 9:39

- possibly it refers to "Abinadab" (BDB 4), mentioned in 1 Sam. 31:2, where #2-3 are not mentioned as sons of
Saul. 1 Samuel 31:32 mentions that Saul and three of his sons were killed by the Philistines (i.e., Jonathan,
Abinadab, and Malchi-shua). Apparently only Ish-bosheth/Eshbaal survived.

verses.zh: 扫罗的妻名叫亚希暖，是亚希玛斯的女儿。扫罗的元帅名叫押尼珥，是尼珥的儿子；尼珥是扫罗的叔叔。
verses.en: The name of Saul’s wife was Ahinoam, the daughter of Ahimaaz. The name of the general in command of his army was Abner son of Ner, Saul’s uncle.[NOTE:1]
notes: 1 Chr 9:35-36 indicates that Jeiel (= Abiel?) had two sons (among others) named Ner and Kish (see also 1 Sam 9:1 and 1 Chr 8:30, where some Greek manuscripts include the name Ner, though it is absent in the Hebrew text). If this Kish was the father of Saul and Ner was the father of Abner, then Saul and Abner were cousins. However, according to 1 Chr 8:33 and 9:39, Ner, not Abiel, was the father of Kish. In this case, Kish and Abner were brothers and Abner was Saul’s uncle. The simplest solution to the problem is to see two men named Kish in the genealogy: Abiel (Jeiel) was the father of Ner and Kish I. Ner was the father of Abner and Kish II. Kish II was the father of Saul. The Kish mentioned in 1 Sam 9:1 was the father of Saul (v. 2) and must be identified as Kish II. In this case the genealogy is “gapped,” with Ner being omitted. Abiel was the grandfather of Kish II.

verses.zh: 扫罗的父亲基士，押尼珥的父亲尼珥，都是亚别的儿子。
verses.en: Kish was the father of Saul, and Ner the father of Abner was the son[NOTE:1] of Abiel.

verses.zh: 扫罗平生常与非利士人大大争战。扫罗遇见有能力的人或勇士，都招募了来跟随他。
verses.en: There was fierce war with the Philistines all the days of Saul. So whenever Saul saw anyone who was a warrior or a brave individual, he would conscript him.
verses.commentary:
14:52 Saul continues to build his standing military.

- Explain the unusual use of "Hebrew" in 1 Sam. 14:21.

- What is Saul trying to do in 1 Sam. 14:33?

- How did the Israeli army "ransom" Jonathan (v. 45)?

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 14:1-5

1Now the day came that Jonathan, the son of Saul, said to the young man who was carrying his armor,
"Come and let us cross over to the Philistines' garrison that is on the other side." But he did not tell his father.
2Saul was staying in the outskirts of Gibeah under the pomegranate tree which is in Migron. And the
people who were with him were about six hundred men, 3and Ahijah, the son of Ahitub,
Ichabod's brother, the son of Phinehas, the son of Eli, the priest of the Lord at Shiloh,
was wearing an ephod. And the people did not know that Jonathan had gone. 4Between the passes by
which Jonathan sought to cross over to the Philistines' garrison, there was a sharp crag on the one side and a sharp
crag on the other side, and the name of the one was Bozez, and the name of the other Seneh. 5The
one crag rose on the north opposite Michmash, and the other on the south opposite Geba.
